name: upgauge-api-rate-limit
description: THE THRESHOLD (issue #19's third acceptance criterion, and #52's second option): block a source IP once it exceeds 1 request/second on /api/, blocking for 10 seconds. A human on /explore triggers a handful of /api/pivot calls a minute; a scraper walking 22,420 route pages does not fit inside 1/s. robots.txt already disallows /api/ to well-behaved crawlers -- this is the backstop for ones that ignore it. The window is 10s because this zone's plan permits no other: the API rejects anything else with 'not entitled to use the period 60, can only use a period among [10]'. The design asked for 60-per-60s; that is the same sustained rate, but 10-in-10s trips on a burst 60-in-60s would have absorbed. The mitigation timeout is 10s for the same reason as the window: 'not entitled to use a mitigation timeout different from 10'. The design asked to block for 60s, so a throttled client resumes six times sooner than intended -- this caps sustained throughput, it is not a wall.

rules.description: Rate limit /api/ to 1 request/second per source IP so a scraper cannot keep the origin awake
